author: Mateusz Pusz

evidence.note: Mateusz Pusz's earlier WG21 paper argues for standardizing a physical quantities and units library for the C++ Standard Library, with the goal of providing 'std::units' with strong types and compile-time dimensional analysis; it implemented and tested the ideas in the mp-units library.
evidence.title: P1935R2: A C++ Approach to Physical Units

evidence.note: The mp-units repository identifies Mateusz Pusz as project founder and lead. The README states mp-units is 'a candidate for ISO standardization for C++29' and cites P3045 as the technical case; it explicitly promotes standardizing a domain-correct quantities and units library.
evidence.title: mp-units GitHub repository

evidence.note: R0 asked the committee to evaluate and accept major design decisions for a quantities and units library based on the mp-units V2 design. By R9 the author reframed the ask around a 'Core Library Framework scope', standardized DejaVu namespace as std, renamed 'expression templates' to 'symbolic expressions', and added magnitude/affine-space/formatting chapters after committee feedback. These show the ask narrowed to a framework-only standardization while specific systems of quantities and units were deferred.
evidence.title: P3045R0: Quantities and units library
evidence.what_changed: Renamed 'expression templates' to 'symbolic expressions'; refactored 'Minimal Viable Product (MVP) scope' to 'Core Library Framework scope'; replaced mp_units namespace with std; rewrote the affine space chapter and added magnitudes; quantity formatting refactored to syntax agreed with Victor Zverovich. The direction (standardize a generic framework, defer specific systems) remained consistent.

evidence.note: In his report from the Croydon 2026 ISO C++ meeting, Mateusz Pusz personally celebrates that LEWG's first review of P3045R7 showed no opposition to the proposed scope (framework, quantity kinds, quantities of the same kind, affine space, and text output). He describes preparing a 200-slide evening session to advocate the design and urges production field trials before C++29.
evidence.title: Report from the Croydon 2026 ISO C++ Committee meeting

evidence.note: C++ on Sea 2023 session by Mateusz Pusz presenting the redesigned mp-units library. He argues for the new design (compile-time dimensional analysis, quantity/unit manipulation), explains why his earlier design failed and why user-defined literals are not a good choice for creating quantities, and discusses language features needed to improve such a library toward standardization.
evidence.title: mp-units: Lessons learned and a new library design - C++ on Sea 2023

evidence.note: A Reddit commenter on the discussion of Mateusz Pusz's 'mp-units: Lessons learned and a new library design' talk argued the design should mature in a library like mp-units rather than be rushed into the standard, citing std::regex and std::format as cautionary examples.
evidence.title: r/cpp discussion of mp-units: Lessons learned and a new library design

position: Mateusz Pusz has consistently and publicly advocated standardizing a C++ quantities and units library built on his mp-units design. From P1935R2 (2020) through P3045R0 to P3045R9, his ask evolved from standardizing physical units with typed quantities and the mp-units design to a framework-only proposal: a generic quantities and units library in the standard library while deferring standardization of specific systems of quantities and units. He honors committee feedback by renaming and descoping when asked (e.g. expression templates to symbolic expressions, MVP scope to Core Library Framework scope, mp_units to std namespace), while retaining the core dimension-, unit-, representation-, quantity-kind-, and affine-space-safe framework. He reinforces the same position publicly through the mp-units project's standardization outreach, conference talks such as C++ on Sea 2023, and committee reports like the Croydon 2026 write-up in which he celebrated LEWG's first poll showing no opposition to the proposed scope.
recommendation: This paper proposes standardizing a generic framework for a C++ quantities and units library in the standard library, providing dimension-, unit-, representation-, quantity-kind-, quantity-, and affine-space-safe abstractions while leaving the standardization of specific systems of quantities and units to subsequent proposals.
title: Quantities and units library
